subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected with 409, skipped, queued, or accepted by default, and should any overlap policy be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The requested behavior changes an external HTTP webhook response contract, retry semantics, session-state admission, and trust-boundary expectations, so automation cannot safely choose the default or compatibility policy.

options.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Keep current 200/runId behavior by default and add a trusted hook/mapping overlap policy such as reject, skip, queue, or parallel with documented active-plus-queued semantics.

options.title: Make 409 The Default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default and accept the migration risk for existing integrations that expect accepted asynchronous hook delivery.

options.title: Defer To Queue Design
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers decide whether durable queued webhook ingestion should own overlap, backpressure, and retry semantics instead.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Keep current 200/runId behavior by default and add a trusted hook/mapping overlap policy such as reject, skip, queue, or parallel with documented active-plus-queued semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest recent history across hook ingress, isolated session behavior, and the prior product-policy framing for this exact issue.
